sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Patil Automation is a capable custom automation integrator, not yet a demonstrated high-return automation-IP compounder. At ₹362.65 on 19 October 2026, the market values its 21,820,800 shares at ₹791.33 crore. FY2026 standalone revenue grew 27.1% to ₹150.05 crore and PAT to ₹15.85 crore, but CFO was negative ₹4.38 crore. Four-year comparable CFO/PAT is only 9.4%. The attractive sector narrative is not enough to overcome weak realized cash and the large additional capital requirement.

BQS 4.80/10, GQS 5.0/10 after the persistent cash cap, IAS NS. The intended new ₹78.65 crore expansion is not underwritten with cash merely because shareholders approved ₹95.95 crore of equity and warrants. Approval, allotment, upfront warrant cash and optional conversion are distinct. Current official shares remain 21,820,800. G3 is Hold for the funding-dependent growth case, not a finding of default. Existing-business deferral is modeled separately and can remain funded under explicit assumptions.

The core question is whether new capacity and working capital can earn healthy incremental returns and cash, rather than simply more reported revenue. Current price is 44.50× reported consolidated owners PAT and 49.94× parent PAT. With only ₹8 crore incremental collateral lock assumed, not verified, the hypothetical funded base produces -5.66% annual return and the bull 9.26%, below the 12% lower hurdle. These are conditional illustrations, not normal expected returns or trade levels. Watch for validated funding, collections and incremental returns before considering the company investment-ready.

REV uses the preselected five year organic proxy, not the more flattering three year window.

BQS weights are 20/20/12/10/12/10/8/8% in GOV/MOAT/REV/DUR/CAP/CASH/BAL/EXEC order. Exact weighted raw and final BQS are 4.80. No renormalization or midpoint imputation occurs.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company engineers and builds welding fixtures, assembly lines, inspection jigs, conveyors and turnkey automation. Customers are buying reliable plant throughput, quality, safety and commissioning, not just metal components. Patil combines mechanical design, fabrication, controls, integration and site execution. Third-party robots and components can be integrated into projects; the available evidence does not establish a proprietary industrial robot OEM or licensable software platform with recurring high-margin revenue.

FY26 parent product revenue ₹145.2444 crore includes welding/assembly equipment and ₹0.2668 crore scrap; services ₹4.8051 crore. No FY26 parent exports were reported, against ₹0.5299 crore in FY25. Presentation references customers in 10+ countries reflect history, not the current export mix. Revenue is project acceptance/delivery driven; cash collection can lag engineering work, materials and inventory. Customer advances help fund execution but are obligations to deliver, not free equity.

Automotive constituted 67% of FY26 revenue in the presentation, versus 88.84% FY25 and 98.30% FY24; non auto 33% is commercially interesting but still project-based. Examples include energy-storage and data-centre-related assembly lines, which are equipment orders rather than ownership of data centres or recurring cloud revenue. Pentaco and Mii add adjacent integration capabilities, not automatic platform economics. A new 90%-owned green energy subsidiary and up-to ₹10 crore support permission widen allocation risk and require a separate investment case.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Mechanism 1: engineering and commissioning know-how can reduce customer downtime and ramp risk. Evidence is delivered custom lines, a decade of operations and management’s repeat-customer claim. Durability depends on experienced engineers, safe handover, project quality and service. Failure mode is loss of technical talent or a capable integrator matching design/service at lower cost. Estimated replication would require experienced teams, reference projects and qualification cycles over years, but no independently verified fixed entry cost/time is supplied.

Mechanism 2: existing customer relationships and familiarity with plant standards can win repeat business. Yet RHP top 10 customers represented 76.67% FY25 revenue, versus 79.51% FY24 and 70.88% FY23; largest 14.55%, top 5 about 57.45%. Orders are purchase-order based, not long term minimum volume commitments. A 10–15% customer loss at 14.5% core EBITDA margin can remove ₹2.2–3.3 crore annual EBITDA before fixed-cost under absorption. This is concentration risk as well as relationship strength.

Mechanism 3: integrated manufacturing and engineering may improve speed/cost, but large facilities and working capital also raise fixed and funding burdens. Top 10 suppliers were 50.75% FY25 purchases, largest 13.34%, without long term contracts. Pricing power is not proven by customization alone. RHP only disclosed a trademark application at that date; no verified patent portfolio, network effects or annuity software economics support a premium platform label. Reputed customers and certifications are not a moat by themselves. Relevant market share and industry growth denominator are ND; management’s discussion of huge BESS/data centre pipelines cannot be converted into a market share claim.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Comparable parent revenue moved ₹63.2963 crore FY21, ₹94.1629 crore FY22, ₹77.8075 crore FY23, ₹115.2796 crore FY24, ₹118.0513 crore FY25 and ₹150.0494 crore FY26. Five-year CAGR is 18.84%; three-year CAGR 24.47%. Ten-year CAGR is ND. FY21 is a pandemic-affected starting period, so FY22→FY26 growth about 12.35% is a useful conservative context, not a replacement chosen after seeing the score. Annual absolute additions and negative FY23 are preserved in the rows.

FY26 parent growth 27.10% added ₹31.9981 crore. Rounded presentation H1 FY26 ₹71.06 crore versus H1 FY25 ₹58.35 crore implies 21.78%; H2 FY26 ₹78.99 crore versus ₹59.70 crore implies 32.31%. The two halves show acceleration, but REV stays 7 without a +1 trajectory adjustment. No FY27 interim financials were authenticated by cutoff; TTM is therefore FY26, not manufactured from future data.

Consolidated FY26 revenue ₹166.5669 crore exceeds parent by ₹16.5175 crore after eliminations. That difference is acquired perimeter, not verified organic growth. Comparing group FY26 to FY25 parent would show 41.10% but mix scopes. Volume, price/mix and new customer contributions are not quantified separately; facilities enabled more projects but do not establish actual recognized revenue at capacity. Material consumption adjusted for WIP leaves manufacturing value-added proxy ₹55.8867 crore FY25 and ₹71.1162 crore FY26, about 47.3–47.4% of sales, supporting real activity growth without claiming this is gross profit. It still contains labour, subcontracting and other costs.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The existing new facility was described as operational in FY26, with management estimating combined revenue capacity ₹250–300 crore. Statements that 80–85% of the shop floor has projects do not mean 80–85% revenue utilization: WIP can occupy space before acceptance and cash. May management described roughly ₹100–118 crore orders and ₹800 crore discussions; these are dated claims, not October bankable backlog. No automatic industry TAM to-company revenue conversion is used.

IPO gross proceeds ₹69.6096 crore originally allocated ₹62.0061 crore capex, ₹4 crore debt, ₹0.5577 crore GCP and ₹3.0458 crore issue cost. March note 38 showed ₹18.47 crore unused capex earmark. September EGM said ₹9.16 crore remained and the facility was completed, proposing working capital redeployment by 31 December 2026. Shareholders approved it October 3. The table heading mislabels ₹9.16 as utilized, but the narrative and percentage identify it as un utilized; model uses explicit narrative, not double counted gross/net proceeds.

The next ₹78.65 crore project is separate: ₹2.50 crore lease, ₹59.64 crore development/shed and ₹16.51 crore infrastructure. Planned issue funding ₹73.74 crore plus internal ₹4.91 crore requires actual receipts and phasing. Corrected raise ₹95.95476 crore comprises ₹51.08436 crore equity and ₹44.8704 crore warrants; initial 25% warrant cash only ₹11.2176 crore, remaining ₹33.6528 crore optional. Our conditional model dates initial net receipt 31 October 2026 and conversion 31 March 2028 solely as assumptions. The cash must arrive before uses; unfunded expansion fails, while deferral has lower ₹300 crore capacity ceiling.

Incremental core NOPAT rose ₹9.9539 crore FY23–26 on ₹91.48–94.76 crore additional capital, about 10.5–10.9%. Before the large plant spend, FY23–25 proxy was 21.6–37.4% depending on cash definition. These are alternative accounting definitions, not universally ordered bounds. Late commissioning can depress near-term returns but does not grant credit for future high returns. Cost-of-capital 12/14/16% sensitivities are judgmental Indian SME post-tax hurdles. The embedded operating/financing bridge prevents cash, subsidiary investments, advances and old liabilities from disappearing. sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Founder-management has application engineering experience and substantial ownership. The October EGM voting record establishes 15,120,000 promoter group shares,69.29% of current capital. Full approved equity/warrant conversion would increase total shares to 25,721,400 and dilute existing holders; promoter warrant participation does not make all new funding received. Institutional allottee names are intended subscribers, not proof of investment completion or investment quality.

FY26 disclosed MD/spouse/CFO salary ₹3.84 crore is about 24% of parent PAT. MD and spouse factory rent aggregates ₹4.6376 crore; identified related family services aggregate ₹4.5429 crore, with additional family salaries. These are commercial transactions reported under related-party controls, not demonstrated diversion. The amounts nevertheless require arm’s-length benchmarking and show why headline promoter alignment is insufficient. Prior Evtric related loan recovery and fresh subsidiary allocations should be monitored for cash recycling and economic purpose.

The full FY25 and FY26 financial opinions and IFC conclusions are unmodified. FY25/FY26 Rule 11 explicitly attests full-year audit trail operation. FY24 original Rule 11 does not contain an equivalent explicit trail statement; absence is not proof the feature was disabled. FY26 CARO reports no default, wilful default, fraud, material one-year liability uncertainty or overdue undisputed dues beyond the threshold. No other company’s bank-return discrepancy or gratuity qualification has been imported. CARO’s statement about FD-backed limits versus note’s partly current-asset-secured OD warrants clarification, not automatic fraud.

CRISIL 7 October 2026 kept B/Stable, A 4 issuer-not-cooperating. It cites non-response and insufficient information, with similar history going back years; this is not an evidenced new default. Rated ₹11.45 crore facilities are not assumed to be current available credit. Management’s May plan to spend remaining ₹18.5 crore within months was later replaced by ₹9.16 crore WC redirect. Facility completion is creditworthy execution, but cash conversion and returns must be demonstrated, not excused by target changes.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The earnings-to-cash bridge is weak over a material profitable period: FY23 CFO ₹0.0127 crore/PAT ₹4.1984 crore, FY24 ₹7.4672/₹7.8372, FY25 ₹0.6300/₹11.7021 and FY26−₹4.3764/₹15.8458. Cumulative CFO ₹3.7335 crore/PAT ₹39.5835 crore is 9.43%. Rental receipts ₹9.6575 crore across four years are classified investing; including them raises conversion to 33.83%, and subtracting financing-classified interest reduces it further. Neither adjustment produces strong cash realization. Fixed asset capex is investing, so it explains weak FCF, not negative CFO.

FY26 inventory rose ₹29.8483 crore, largely project WIP; receivables fell ₹5.9713 crore but remained ₹43.9606 crore. Supplier advances rose from ₹0.1936 crore to ₹7.8933 crore; cashflow identifies ₹7.0157 crore capital advances, analytically separated from operating NWC rather than paid again. Supplier ledger mapping remains an assumption. Receivables older than one year ₹4.5241 crore had zero provision; engineering acceptance claims need collection evidence. Trade payables ₹26.8134 crore and customer advances ₹14.3815 crore fund part of the cycle. MSME unpaid interest ₹0.0584 crore is reserved once, not ignored.

Gross cash/deposits ₹38.4356 crore comprised ₹0.6825 crore bank/hand, ₹11.9811 crore 3–12 month FD and ₹25.7720 crore long FD. IPO earmark ₹18.47 crore is not general cash. ₹14.7094 crore OD is specifically FD-backed and ₹3.9285 crore secured by current/immovable assets. We assume ₹16.3438 crore collateral at 90% advance solely for stress modeling; actual FD lien/IPO overlap is not disclosed. Non overlap and 0/8/12/16.34/19.97 crore incremental lock cases bound availability, without pretending every FD is liquid. Future OD rollover is assumed, not an undrawn facility.

Old net income tax ₹0.9689 crore, statutory ₹0.4490 crore, employee ₹1.7291 crore, short gratuity ₹0.0731 crore and MSME interest ₹0.0584 crore are paid once on explicit dates. Long gratuity ₹1.3036 crore is runoff over five years; ₹0.9015 crore rental security deposit is reserved at terminal. Other payables ₹2.0674 crore sit in NWC, not duplicated as an extra cash payment. DTA ₹1.3613 crore is not cash. Bank guarantees ₹1.4728 crore are contingent, not regular borrowings. Cash model preserves maintenance capex, taxes, interest, cash floor and ownership dilution.

FY26 core EBITDA ₹19.9212 crore excludes ₹6.768 crore other income. Parent PAT contains ₹0.6842 crore deferred tax benefit; current tax plus prior-tax ₹5.4880 crore differs from P&L net tax. Reported weighted EPS ₹7.71 is not current-share EPS ₹7.2618. Group PAT ₹19.0743 crore includes ₹1.2914 crore NCI; owners ₹17.7829 crore must be used for P/E. The NCI bridge is internally reconciled: closing aggregate subsidiary net worth ₹3.7415295 crore less acquisition net worth ₹0.5131 crore gives post-acquisition increase ₹3.2284295 crore;40% is ₹1.2913718 crore, matching NCI profit. Closing NCI 40% is ₹1.4966118 crore. AOC 1 full-year PAT ₹1.0997314 crore covers a different period; implied pre-acquisition losses and capital movements need further clarification, not automatic misstatement. The forward case uses the parent and subsidiaries at cost, without claiming group growth organic.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Market cap ₹791.3313 crore/current parent PAT ₹15.8458 crore implies 49.94× P/E; reported group owners PAT ₹17.7829 crore gives 44.50× subject to different pre/post-acquisition subsidiary periods. Current-share parent EPS ₹7.2618 and group owners EPS ₹8.1495 avoid understating multiples by using weighted EPS. Parent EV after all March gross cash and ₹3.65 croresubsidiary/bankinvestmentsis ₹767.88 crore,38.55× core EBITDA. All-cash net EV does not imply cash availability. No separate value for operating property is added when its rent remains capitalized.

Model terminal date is 19 October 2031, exactly 4.999316 years after entry under actual days/365.25. Audited March 2026 balances roll through dated quarterly intervals, including entry and hypothetical fundraise events; no March 2032 cash leaks into terminal. Bear/base/bull run rate growth 8/20/30%, core EBITDA margins 10.5/14.5/16%, operating NWC 45/35/30% and exit EV/NOPAT 10/16/22× are assumptions, not targets. Recurring maintenance capex 3/3/4% of sales continues through terminal; rent excludes ₹0.606 crore intragroup receipts, properties are not separately revalued. Forward capacity caps ₹300 crore without new expansion, ₹600 crore with it, the latter an analytical assumption not guidance.

Unfunded expansion has no future equity/warrant cash and fails in all three cases. Approved funding paths assume ₹62.30196 crore gross initial cash on 31 October 2026,1.5% fees, and optional ₹33.6528 crore on 31 March 2028 with warrant shares. These hypothetical receipts are not labeled available. All main paths fail conservative pre-receipt trough checks; their returns remain null. Only the lower-lock ₹8 crore availability alternative is solvent. Its funded base conditional terminal ₹270.99 gives-5.66%; bull ₹564.75 gives 9.26%. Bear requires cash before the first modeled quarter ending June 2026 under its selected assumptions, so all non-rescue returns remain null even if later funding arrives. This is a model sensitivity, not observed distress.

Conditional 12/15/18% hurdle prices, full 56 two-way stress rows, linked funded reverse-solvers and whole-share pre-funded rescues are embedded. Rescue equity is priced at 75% of entry price with 2% fees, timed before interval uses, reconciles gross/net and dilution, and is never presented as committed money. The ordinary expected return and ordinary entry price remain NS under G3. A finite funded solver crossing is required; tested upper growth endpoints are not reported as solutions. When existing capacity caps revenue, the model cannot conjure free growth by deferring capex.

Directly comparable peer multiples are ND because a matched set of project integrators with similar accounting scope and funding risk was not authenticated. Exit multiples are explicit valuation sensitivities, not claims about a proven robotics-IP peer premium.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
A plausible bear path starts with OEM project deferrals or loss of a large customer, followed by inventory/WIP residing longer on the shop floor. Certification and acceptance delays increase capital tied up, while fixed engineering staff and facilities cannot be reduced instantly. Receivable ageing then converts from timing risk into credit loss. Initial economic damage is not merely a lower market multiple: cash funding needs rise and may force expensive capital, capex deferral or loss making project completion.

The model’s bear 8% growth,10.5% core margin and 45% operating NWC breaches ₹1.5 crore cash reserve before entry. Neither approved later fundraising nor assumed optional warrants may repair that pre-entry failure without an explicit bridge. Unfunded new expansion requires roughly ₹79 crore peak additional cash in the illustrative bear case. That number is not a statement of actual arrears: it results of chosen liens, reserves, growth and project phasing. Deferral removes new capex but cannot cure all bear working capital pressure. Sensitivities include eligible IPO use, collateral overlap, capex overruns, WC days, warrant non exercise and ₹10 crore green energy support.

Permanent loss can also arise without insolvency. Paying roughly 45–50× earnings for an integrator whose growth requires repeated capital can produce poor per-share returns despite higher revenue. Full approved issuance expands shares by 17.88% and reduces an existing holder’s percentage by 15.16% before any rescue. Governance harm could arise if related transactions or new subsidiaries receive capital without competitive economic returns; current disclosures do not prove such abuse. Thesis-breaking evidence would be auditor qualification, unexplained fund movement, actual payment default, uncollectible receivables or continued cash conversion under 30% despite new capacity maturation.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold returns require business and per-share value creation, not just surviving an industry boom. At current ₹362.65, target prices are ₹1,813.25 and ₹3,626.50. With 25,721,400 fully converted shares, those prices require equity values about ₹4,664 crore and ₹9,328 crore. The embedded grid translates these into unlevered NOPAT and revenue needs at 12/16/22× exit EV/NOPAT,25.17% tax and base operating margins. It assumes zero net debt/excess cash only for the simple arithmetic feasibility grid and explicitly labels that limitation.

The linked reverse underwriting separately solves the actual dated cash, capex, financing, share count and terminal reserve model for 12/15/18% return hurdles. It accepts only finite funded bracket crossings and records residuals. Infeasible cases remain null, not the maximum growth tested. Cash conversion and capacity constraints mean raising growth can worsen funding before improving terminal value. The ₹600 crore expanded capacity ceiling is not already contracted output and would itself require strong execution.

On current evidence,5× is not a credible base case and 10× is far more demanding. Both would need several rounds of value-accretive expansion, much higher capital productivity and cash conversion, durable qualification advantages, successful diversification and little economic dilution. Assuming a higher terminal multiple for an unproven IP narrative would not make those outcomes operationally credible. Treat the grid as what must be true, not probabilities or price predictions.

The linked scan also explicitly tests 5× and 10× per-share targets. At 0–80% annual growth, the ₹600 crore capacity ceiling and ₹8 crore incremental-lock availability assumption produce no finite funded crossing for those targets or the 12/15/18% hurdles at 12/16/22/30× terminal NOPAT. This is a bounded model result, not proof that any conceivable future expansion is impossible.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
First, obtain actual allotment documents, net bank receipt and updated share capital for the September proposal. Separately track equity ₹51.08436 crore,25% warrant ₹11.2176 crore and optional 75%₹33.6528 crore; a shareholder vote or allottee name is not cash. Update funding dates and cash trough before updating return estimates. Confirm which IPO ₹9.16 crore was legally used for WCby 31 December 2026 and which FD remains pledged.

Second, compare upcoming H1 FY27 and FY27 parent revenue, core margins and CFO with stated growth. Require bank-collected reduction in aged receivables, WIP milestone conversion and no repeated supplier advance build. Track CFO/PAT above 80% over at least two comparable periods, while including interest and rental classification consistently. Improvement should come from collections and project economics, not stretching MSME payables or new customer advances to fund old projects.

Third, measure capital deployment and returns: commissioning dates, remaining cash obligations, capex advances, capacity throughput and excess space. Ask for plant-level returns or matured cohort data, but do not withhold all judgment solely because private project IRRs are not provided. Seek parent incremental NOPAT return above 12–16% range on cash consistent capital and falling ONWC/sales. Require clear arm’s-length related rent/services, green energy support cap, subsidiary consolidation reconciliation and restored rating cooperation.

Finally, recheck tradeability before execution: latest series, surveillance, circuit bands, bid queue, spread and 600-share lot. A ₹5 lakh reference cannot be exactly held:2 lots cost ₹4.3518 lakh,3 lots ₹6.5277 lakh. Positioning must fit actual risk capacity; turnover-derived 0.66 days is not a promise to liquidate.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: expanding custom automation integrator with unproven post-expansion cash returns. This is a financing-gated watchlist, not a proven compounder. Observe rather than assign an ordinary investable ranking until the funding-dependent expansion is credibly financed. Commercial progress is real, but current valuation demands more than revenue growth and capacity announcements.

G3 Hold and R NS keep the IAS point score, ordinary IRR and ordinary entry price absent. BQS 4.8 and capped GQS 5.0 describe current business economics and evidence, not a price-independent endorsement. Conditional prices require the specifically stated funding and deposit-availability assumptions. Higher conviction would require actual receipts, credible capital phasing, matured incremental returns and sustained collections, not merely a higher share price or a prominent investor name.

This is general research, not personalized portfolio advice or a trade recommendation. SME shares can be difficult to exit and can permanently lose capital.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence includes the complete FY2026 and FY2025 annual reports, main audit opinions and annexures; original FY2021–FY2024 statutory financial statements; the June 2025 RHP and restatement bridges; May 2026 results, presentation and call; September board notice and corrigendum; October EGM proceedings and final voting results; CRISIL's October 7 rationale; and official NSE security, daily trading and holiday records. Source links, financial periods, document dates and precise page references accompany the evidence.

Important open questions remain: actual preferential allotment and cash receipt; FD maturity, lien and IPO overlap; capital-advance supplier mapping and capital creditors; subsidiary pre- and post-acquisition results and capital movements; order acceptance and collection dates; the productivity and phasing of new investment; related-party commercial fairness; green-energy support; and current execution liquidity. The NCI arithmetic reconciles to the post-acquisition net-worth bridge, so the different full-year AOC 1 figures are not by themselves a demonstrated error.

Historical values, calculations and dated scenarios are supplied in the accompanying canonical data. Unknown facts are ND or NS, never a neutral score or an undisclosed funding plug. All forward growth, margin, working-capital, capacity, cash-reserve, financing-date and exit-multiple assumptions are explicit. The 75%-of-reference rescue price is hypothetical, not a proven financeable distress price; a lower price requires more shares and greater dilution. Data after 20 October 2026 is excluded.

assumptions_and_limits:
Primary evidence includes the complete FY2026 and FY2025 annual reports, main audit opinions and annexures; original FY2021–FY2024 statutory financial statements; the June 2025 RHP and restatement bridges; May 2026 results, presentation and call; September board notice and corrigendum; October EGM proceedings and final voting results; CRISIL's October 7 rationale; and official NSE security, daily trading and holiday records. Source links, financial periods, document dates and precise page references accompany the evidence.

Important open questions remain: actual preferential allotment and cash receipt; FD maturity, lien and IPO overlap; capital-advance supplier mapping and capital creditors; subsidiary pre- and post-acquisition results and capital movements; order acceptance and collection dates; the productivity and phasing of new investment; related-party commercial fairness; green-energy support; and current execution liquidity. The NCI arithmetic reconciles to the post-acquisition net-worth bridge, so the different full-year AOC 1 figures are not by themselves a demonstrated error.

Historical values, calculations and dated scenarios are supplied in the accompanying canonical data. Unknown facts are ND or NS, never a neutral score or an undisclosed funding plug. All forward growth, margin, working-capital, capacity, cash-reserve, financing-date and exit-multiple assumptions are explicit. The 75%-of-reference rescue price is hypothetical, not a proven financeable distress price; a lower price requires more shares and greater dilution. Data after 20 October 2026 is excluded.
summary:
Patil Automation is a capable custom automation integrator, not yet a demonstrated high-return automation-IP compounder. At ₹362.65 on 19 October 2026, the market values its 21,820,800 shares at ₹791.33 crore. FY2026 standalone revenue grew 27.1% to ₹150.05 crore and PAT to ₹15.85 crore, but CFO was negative ₹4.38 crore. Four-year comparable CFO/PAT is only 9.4%. The attractive sector narrative is not enough to overcome weak realized cash and the large additional capital requirement.

BQS 4.80/10, GQS 5.0/10 after the persistent cash cap, IAS NS. The intended new ₹78.65 crore expansion is not underwritten with cash merely because shareholders approved ₹95.95 crore of equity and warrants. Approval, allotment, upfront warrant cash and optional conversion are distinct. Current official shares remain 21,820,800. G3 is Hold for the funding-dependent growth case, not a finding of default. Existing-business deferral is modeled separately and can remain funded under explicit assumptions.

The core question is whether new capacity and working capital can earn healthy incremental returns and cash, rather than simply more reported revenue. Current price is 44.50× reported consolidated owners PAT and 49.94× parent PAT. With only ₹8 crore incremental collateral lock assumed, not verified, the hypothetical funded base produces -5.66% annual return and the bull 9.26%, below the 12% lower hurdle. These are conditional illustrations, not normal expected returns or trade levels. Watch for validated funding, collections and incremental returns before considering the company investment-ready.
